en.html: Hikaru was—probably right. Probably this was the most practical plan available. Fully armed infantry. Possibly guns and vehicles too. Then a tsurugi on top of everything. And to stop this lot, what did I have? One body. Bas. Worse, my foster mother's teaching had not conveniently vanished. You must not kill. Stop the armed men, and kindly return all of them alive. ...Haan. For that, a tsurugi was necessary after all. Its power could disable ordinary weapons without much difficulty. Probably I could spare the soldiers too. Another tsurugi would leave no such comfortable margin—but show equal force, and perhaps a negotiation became possible. Practical. The argument stood on both feet. Why, then, could I not bring myself to agree...?◆ Probably because I had seen that tsurugi. That foulness. Skin rising in bumps before the mind had finished objecting. Taking such a thing out into the world—no, that worry would not leave me. But. ...Lekin...
en.text:
Hikaru was—probably right.
Probably this was the most practical plan available.

Fully armed infantry. Possibly guns and vehicles too.
Then a tsurugi on top of everything.

And to stop this lot, what did I have? One body. Bas.
Worse, my foster mother's teaching had not conveniently vanished.

You must not kill.

Stop the armed men, and kindly return all of them alive.
...Haan. For that, a tsurugi was necessary after all.

Its power could disable ordinary weapons without much difficulty. Probably I could spare the soldiers too.
Another tsurugi would leave no such comfortable margin—but show equal force, and perhaps a negotiation became possible.

Practical. The argument stood on both feet.

Why, then, could I not bring myself to agree...?◆

Probably because I had seen that tsurugi.

That foulness. Skin rising in bumps before the mind had finished objecting.
Taking such a thing out into the world—no, that worry would not leave me.

But.
...Lekin...

光の言うことは――おそらく正しい。
　おそらく……この状況下では最も現実的なプランだ。

　完全武装の歩兵。あるいは更に砲、車両。
　そして劒冑。

　身体一つでどうやって止められよう。
　しかも――俺は養母の教えを思い出していた。

　殺してはならない。

　殺さずに、武装集団を制止せねばならない。
　……やはり、劒冑は必要だった。

　劒冑の力があれば、通常兵器の無力化は難しくない。
兵士を殺さずに済ませる事も、おそらくできる。
　同じ劒冑に対してはそんな余裕などなかろうが――
対等の戦力を示せば交渉に持ち込む事はできそうだ。

　現実的である。

　それでも、どうしても同意に二の足を踏むのは……◆

　
　あの劒冑を見ているからだろう。

　肌が粟立つまでの禍々しさ。
　あんなものを持ち出すことに、懸念は拭えない。

　しかし。
　……しかし……

I looked at my palm. At the hand that had gone through all that training.

The Yoshino Style Rules of Engagement were an armoured warrior's art.
Then surely I could do it. The training had not been for decorating my hands...!

　やってやれない事はない筈だ……！

en.html: She even answered me properly while opening the doors. Full courtesy, not one bit of obedience. Those heavy doors swung aside as though the weight had been somebody's misunderstanding. And inside— the tsurugi. Two suits of armour. A silver queen ant, and¦ a deep crimson spider.
en.text:
She even answered me properly while opening the doors. Full courtesy, not one bit of obedience.
Those heavy doors swung aside as though the weight had been somebody's misunderstanding.

And inside—
the tsurugi.

Two suits of armour.

A silver queen ant, and¦
a deep crimson spider.

en.html:
I tried to hurry to her. My feet hurried into a stumble instead.
That air of calamity, that smell of ill omen—the force coming off those tsurugi had not become any more bearable on a second viewing.

Hikaru, meanwhile, seemed entirely unbothered.
She simply went over and held a hand above the great silver ant.

en.html:
I knew what this meant.
Not only what would happen. Why it would happen. The knowledge was sitting in my brain, explaining everything with absolutely useless punctuality.

—Hikaru had ALREADY bonded with that tsurugi!?

I could only stare.
Silver fragments glittered around her. She narrowed her eyes as though enjoying their company, and her fingers moved through the air, leisurely, gracefully.

The Armoring Stance!

en.html:
Only putting it on.
For that much activity, THIS much destruction?

What kind of power was inside that tsurugi?
Even imagining it sent a shiver down my spine.

The blast had hit me, but I was unhurt.
My foster mother too. Good luck—no. Probably Hikaru had taken care of that.

...Then standing here like a stunned ullu was not an option.

I had to follow.
Stopping Hikaru had failed. Chasing her, at least, had to begin now.

I looked at the tsurugi still there.
So close to that blast, and not a scratch. The bloody thing had not even fallen over.

It was telling me something I did not particularly wish to hear: its power was no less than the silver ant's...

　あの劒冑はどれほどの<ruby>異能<rt>ちから</rt></ruby>を有しているのか。
　想像するだに、背筋が震えた。

　爆風は浴びたが、俺の身体に傷はない。
　養母も同様だ。幸いにも――いや。光が配慮してく
れたのだろう。

　……ならば、のんびり呆けている場合ではなかった。

　俺も続かねばならない。
　光を止め損ねてしまった以上、すぐにも追わねば。

　残った一領の劒冑を見やる。
　あの暴発の至近距離にありながら、損傷も無ければ
倒れてさえいなかった。

　その事実は、白銀の蟻に劣らぬ力の存在を否が応に
も知らしめる……。

en.html:
My name is Muramasa.

Meet a demon, cut the demon.

Meet a Buddha, cut the Buddha.

I am not good.

I do not obey justice.

I walk no righteous path.

I cut down right and wrong together.

I am a single blade of calamity.

You who seek a pact with me—
Are you prepared to become, with me, a blade of calamity?

If not, leave.

If so—
